intro: Read a Spanish job advert and learn vocabulary for applications, working conditions and employment.
p.la oferta de trabajo: the job vacancy; the job advert
p.la oferta de trabajo.nota: Depending on context, this can refer to a vacancy or the advert announcing it.
p.despedir.nota: In some present-tense forms, e changes to i: despido, despides, despide, despiden; the nosotros and vosotros forms keep e: despedimos, despedís.
p.el presupuesto: the budget; the estimate or quote
p.el presupuesto.nota: In a service or business context, a presupuesto is often an estimate or quote for work.
p.en prácticas: as an intern, as a trainee
p.autónomo.nota: Used as a noun or adjective for someone self-employed; the feminine form is autónoma.
p.se requiere.nota: In a job advert, the verb agrees with the following noun: se requiere experiencia; se requieren dos años de experiencia.
p.se ofrece.nota: In a job advert, the verb agrees with the following noun: se ofrece un contrato; se ofrecen buenas condiciones.
p.el candidato.nota: The feminine form is la candidata.
p.el empleado.nota: The feminine form is la empleada.
p.el estudiante en prácticas.nota: The feminine form is la estudiante en prácticas.
p.el funcionario.nota: The feminine form is la funcionaria.
b1.texto:
Many job adverts use **se** to leave the employer unnamed: **se busca una persona**; **se buscan dos personas**. In this pattern, the verb agrees with the noun that follows. You may also see **se requiere** experiencia, **se ofrece** un contrato or **se valorará** el inglés.

A vacancy may require **experiencia**, **formación**, **idiomas**, **disponibilidad** or a **carné de conducir**. It may offer a **contrato**, a **sueldo**, a flexible **horario**, training paid for by the company or the possibility of **ascenso**. Conditions vary from one job to another.

The application steps are to **enviar el currículum** and a covering letter, **acudir a una entrevista** and, if selected, **firmar el contrato**. Later, someone may **despedirte**; you may **dimitir** or **jubilarte**.

A worker may be **empleado/a**, **estudiante en prácticas**, **autónomo/a** or **funcionario/a**. In an office, you can prepare an **informe**, a **presupuesto** or a **presentación**, and work in **el departamento de ventas**, **el de contabilidad** or **el de recursos humanos**.
b2.f0: Transport company seeks an administrative assistant for its Valencia office.
b2.f1: At least two years of experience and a good level of English are required.
b2.f2: The candidate will deal with customers and prepare reports and estimates.
b2.f3: A one-year contract with flexible hours and training paid for by the company is offered.
b2.f4: There is a possibility of promotion for anyone who shows interest.
b2.f5: Applicants should send their CV and a covering letter to the human resources department.
b4.pregunta: Complete the advert: experience is required.
b5.pregunta: Someone who works for himself is…
b6.o1: They said goodbye to him yesterday.
b6.o1.explicacion: That would be se despidieron de él.
b7.pregunta: According to the advert, what must candidates send?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Su currículum y una carta de presentación.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Those are tasks of the job.
b7.o2.refuerzo: The advert does not ask for these.
b8.pregunta: Complete: promotion for anyone who shows interest.
b8.o1.refuerzo: Quien refers to nobody in particular yet.
b10.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write a short covering letter for a job you would like.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Answer aloud the classic interview questions: tell me about yourself, your strengths, your weaknesses, why this job.
b11.pregunta: Complete: Two people are wanted for the position.
b11.o0.refuerzo: Use singular with one person: Se busca una persona.
b11.o1.refuerzo: The verb agrees with the plural noun personas.
b11.o2.refuerzo: An infinitive or participle cannot complete this advert.
